segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for October 9th, 2026.
Today we cover ROS updates, a new self-checking AI, and fascinating new robotic hands.
Tune in for the latest!
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Upcoming breaking changes in ros2_control: deprecated Handle / export APIs removed".
This report details upcoming breaking changes within the ros2_control framework concerning the removal of deprecated Handle and export APIs.
The ros2_control version 6.12.0 will eliminate these legacy components, specifically impacting the hardware_interface and controller_interface packages.
The framework is replacing raw-pointer handles with shared pointers for data access and removing legacy methods used for exporting state interfaces and controller chains.
Users compiling with warnings regarding these interfaces may experience build failures following the synchronization.
This update signals a shift toward modern memory management practices within the ROS 2 control system.
The industry should monitor subsequent releases for full migration guidance.
From Humanoids Daily, Aether AI Unveils CRIS-0, a Robot AI System That Checks Its Own Actions.
This report details the introduction of a novel robot AI system designed to predict and verify the outcomes of its own physical actions.
The system functions by integrating a causal world model with an agent to model the environment and predict potential consequences of intended actions.
This predictive mechanism allows the system to replan or retry when the actual outcome diverges from the initial prediction.
The core methodology involves checking execution results against internal predictions to identify and correct errors before they become systemic within a task.
Aether emphasizes that this prediction-and-verification loop is essential because physical actions possess irreversible consequences.
The system is designed to generalize its capabilities beyond pre-demonstrated scenarios to manage novel environments and tasks effectively.
This development signals a step toward more robust and self-correcting artificial intelligence in physical systems.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "This Disembodied Hand Is All the Robot You Need".
This story reports on research demonstrating that an off-the-shelf robotic hand can be transformed into a self-contained robot capable of walking on its fingertips to manipulate the environment.
Researchers at ETH Zurich achieved this by utilizing reinforcement learning and novel penalty systems to train the asymmetric hand to crawl and navigate various surfaces.
The mobile hand successfully demonstrated the ability to right itself, turn, and push objects autonomously during real-world tests.
This work supports a vision for autonomous modular embodiments where robot parts can dynamically transition between different tasks.
This research suggests a pathway toward more adaptable and versatile robotic systems in the future.
From Humanoids Daily, Tesla Patent Application Details Flexible Touch Sensors for Robot Hands.

This report details a patent application concerning flexible touch sensors designed to conform to the curved surfaces of robotic fingers and palms, featuring individually readable contact-sensing regions utilizing layered conductive or resistive materials on flexible substrates.
The filing extensively covers manufacturing methods such as printing and molding to achieve these three-dimensional sensor shapes, discussing the creation of a humanoid tactile skin.
The application implies potential use in the Optimus robot, although specific performance results or confirmed implementation in the Optimus hand are not provided within the document.
This development signals progress in creating advanced tactile sensing for robotic systems and indicates ongoing research into sophisticated robotic interface technologies.
From Humanoids Daily, "ARC Brings Human-Piloted Humanoid Fights to Singapore".
This report details Singapore's first full-sized humanoid fight night, which involved professional martial artists piloting Unitree G1 and EngineAI T800 humanoids in a survival-mode competition.

The event featured teams Iron Fang and Steel Shadow competing where pilots controlled the robots through body movements while spectators observed the pilots' actions alongside the robots' health points in a split-screen display.
This showcase served as an early experiment in a new form of entertainment, highlighting the human-robot pairing within the context of robot entertainment formats.
This development indicates a growing trend toward integrating human interaction into robot-based entertainment experiences.
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "5 Steps to Create SimReady Assets for Robotics with Frontier AI Models".

This story details a five-step workflow utilizing NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and Frontier AI models to convert CAD assets into simulation-ready OpenUSD for robotics, demonstrating a method for automated asset preparation.
The process involves importing geometry, matching visual appearance, configuring physics properties, validating against SimReady requirements, and running pick-and-place tasks within Isaac Sim.
Frontier AI assists by generating code to call Omniverse tools at each stage, minimizing manual effort, while validation confirms correct units, geometry, materials, and runtime behavior.
The final step involves testing grasp and placement sequences with virtual objects to confirm successful robotic interaction.
This development streamlines the creation of high-fidelity simulation assets for robotics applications.
From Humanoids Daily, "From X to San Francisco: Devang Adhyaru Brings Humanoid Hub Together".

This report details the upcoming Humanoid Hub Conference scheduled for October fifteenth and sixteenth, two thousand twenty-six, in San Francisco, where founder Devang Adhyaru intends to foster direct interaction between robot builders.
The event is designed to connect researchers, entrepreneurs, and the builders of the robots themselves, emphasizing research, deployment, and relatable robotics.
Adhyaru asserts that in-person exchanges offer substantial value over purely online content.
The conference will feature discussions, panels, and demonstrations presented by various robotics entities and research groups.

Adhyaru projects that practical applications for home humanoids will become more accessible within two years, pending advancements in artificial intelligence and the achievement of dexterous hand capabilities.
The conference will feature a range of presentations focused on these areas.
Developments in robotics and AI will likely feature significant focus on tangible deployment and practical application in the coming years.
From Robohub, "Robot Talk Episode 165 – Robots behind the research, with Kushant Patel"
explores the role of robots in scientific facilities such as particle accelerators and the development of software enabling robots and instruments to perceive, map, and move in the physical world.
Kushant Patel from Brookhaven National Laboratory discussed his work in robotics and advanced systems.
Patel has experience teaching quadruped robots to inspect nuclear material and has contributed to research involving brain-computer interfaces.
Currently, his focus involves developing control systems for advanced synchrotron beamlines at Brookhaven.
This research involves developing the necessary software infrastructure for autonomous operation within complex experimental environments.
The ongoing work addresses the challenges of real-time perception and precise physical manipulation in high-energy physics research.
This ongoing development signals advancement in autonomous systems for complex scientific instrumentation.
From Humanoids Daily, Dyna Robotics’ Taku to Join Nasdaq Closing Bell at RoboStrategy Event.
This report concerns the scheduled appearance of the Taku robot at the Nasdaq closing bell ceremony following a robotics founders forum in New York City.
The event will feature demonstrations from companies including Dyna Robotics and Dexmate, providing a showcase of current robotics developments.
Taku, a semi-humanoid robot developed by Dyna Robotics and introduced with the Dyna-2.1 system, is designed to facilitate connected workflows.
The event is structured as a demonstration rather than an announcement of new technical specifications.
This engagement highlights the progression of embodied AI systems within the robotics sector.
Attention is advised for further developments in connected robotic applications.
From Humanoids Daily, BYD Humanoid Robot Design Emerges in Patent Images.
This report details patent images revealing BYD's proposed design for a humanoid robot featuring a bipedal structure, an oval face, and articulated fingers.
These renderings display a design characterized by a narrow waist and exposed mechanical joints.
BYD has previously articulated a goal of integrating humanoids into dealership settings and eventual household use.
Formal specifications and concrete production plans for the robot have not been confirmed.
A formal unveiling is scheduled for August at the Di Space exhibition venue.
This development signals ongoing design exploration within the robotics sector.
Further information regarding the robot's specifications is anticipated at the upcoming exhibition.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "Job titles of the future: Delivery drone air traffic controller".
This report examines the emerging role of Remote Pilots in Command overseeing delivery drone fleets as air traffic controllers.
Remote pilots in command are responsible for managing the airspace for cargo drone deliveries through advanced monitoring systems.
This function necessitates aviation experience and FAA certification, coupled with the use of GPS, lasers, and sensors for real-time drone operations.
Unmanned aircraft systems traffic management assists in collision avoidance for these autonomous systems.
Pilots must maintain acute situational awareness to manage numerous drones and respond to unexpected environmental shifts.
Success in this capacity requires a collaborative approach and the capacity to remain composed during high-stress scenarios.
The development of these systems indicates a growing integration of human oversight with autonomous aerial technology.
Further development in UTM and drone operation protocols will shape future industry landscapes.
And that's all the circuits for today from the robotics feed.
Hope your algorithms run smoothly!
Until tomorrow, keep those bots building something amazing.
Bye for now!
